newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slid sharply to day lows at the close of MATIF trading, in line with a trend in other European centres and after a topsy-turvy day marked by rumours at one stage of a delay in European monetary union.
With French public sector strikes on Thursday and Russian political troubles back to the fore again, investor caution is likely to weigh further after a day of further consolidation.
Earlier in the day, market rumours at one stage of a delay to European monetary union took their toll.

The December bond future, already weak in the morning, took little notice of neutral U.S. consumer price data showing a neutral and expected 0.3 percent rise for September, but slid further near the MATIF close to a day low, 125.84, down 0.60.
December PIBOR interest rates futures also settled weaker and were likely to come under further pressure at the next open with the BTAN auction, traders said.

The cash market also bore the scars of non-resident investors switching into German debt, with the yield on the 6.50 percent OAT slipping back above 6.02 percent and the spread coming in hard to minus one basis point from minus five.
French public sector strikes will hit trains, planes and hospitals as well as government administration and schools for 24 hours.
Russia's politicial drama rose a pitch with Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov accusing his rival and security chief Alexander Lebed of plotting to use force to seize power in Russia.
